message.content: Xavier Becerra presents the stronger option for California governor this November. On Gaza, he called for a ceasefire, hostage release, expanded humanitarian aid, and a two-state solution at the World Health Assembly in May 2024, and in 2025 criticized Netanyahu's conduct and demanded international accountability, though he did not call the campaign a genocide and has not backed blocking weapons transfers to Israel. In a 2026 debate he referred to the U.S.-Israeli war in Iran as illegal, a remark the reporting qualified as criticizing the war's form. CAIR Action and Muslim Democrats of Southern California endorse him. Steve Hilton, by contrast, was openly optimistic after Israel struck Iranian nuclear sites in 2025, supports U.S.-funded military aid to Israel, pledged legal action against California cities over BDS, and frames the conflict as an intra-party anti-Semitism issue. Vote for Peace rates Hilton Opposed. The Union of American Physicians and Dentists and Alameda County Jewish Democratic Club back Becerra. His platform centers healthcare, housing, cost-of-living relief, wildfire prevention, and AI governance, statewide priorities that define this race.
